title: Modules & Imports
lead: Each .xr file is a module. import/export must be top-level. The compiler builds a dependency DAG, topologically sorts it, and resolves selective imports to O(1) slot access at runtime.

sections.heading: Imports
sections.markdown: import declarations must appear at module top level. Bare identifiers resolve to stdlib; quoted paths resolve relative to the current file or project root. Dynamic import is not supported.

sections.heading: Exports
sections.markdown: export declarations must appear at module top level. export var is not supported — use export const. Re-exports (named and wildcard) aggregate submodule APIs.

sections.heading: Module graph & circular dependencies
sections.markdown: The compiler builds a module dependency DAG from all import declarations. Circular dependencies are a compile error. Modules initialize in topological order. Selective imports resolve to fixed module index + export slot at compile time.

sections.heading: Published Source definitions
sections.markdown: Persistent Source checking receives only its owner's published Checked Program and registered bindings. Session inputs share an explicit lexical scope while definitions retain their birth modules and private visibility. Runtime receiving requires the actual Source map, exact specialized/Lowered Program proof and the same retained runtime Domain. Budgeted routes preserve actual birth slots and skip only completed birth initialization; reads retain ordinary permissions, publication checks and value admission. Authenticated stored-type roots receive existing identities through acyclic arena ownership; equal shapes grant nothing, and carriers retain their actual birth type and arena. Cell and Array operations use actual storage and per-edge arenas without granting Domain, publication, borrow or call authority. Old Cell side effects survive candidate abort. Complete Class/Array coverage, closures, full G2/G3 and paired REPL publication remain unfinished. See compilation pipeline section17.67.
